prompt.context_jp: 薫は身を乗り出し、田所はグラスを口元で止め、瀬川___目を丸くしてメイの言葉の続きを待っていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 瀬川___目を丸くして…
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that fits the listing context of three colleagues' reactions.

feedback.correct_en: The sentence lists three people's parallel reactions (薫は / 田所は / 瀬川は), each marked as a topic in a contrastive listing. は fits this balanced parallel structure.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would mark Segawa as new information, breaking the parallel listing. を is wrong grammatically here — 瀬川 is the subject of 待っていた, not the object.

contrast_examples.jp: 父は新聞を読み、母はお茶を入れる。
contrast_examples.en: Dad reads the paper, Mom makes tea.

contrast_examples.jp: 誰が来たの？—瀬川が来たよ。
contrast_examples.en: Who came? — Segawa came. (new info → が)

prompt.context_jp: 話が本題に近づくにつれ、メイの声___少しずつ弾んでしまうのを、彼女自身が抑えきれずにいた。
prompt.prompt_jp: メイの声___少しずつ弾んでしまう…
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the particle for the subordinate clause subject.

feedback.correct_en: Inside a のを-nominalized clause, the subject takes が, not は. Also it reports a new observed event (her voice becoming lively), which is typical が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は cannot be used as the subject within a subordinate/nominalized clause like this; it would make the clause ungrammatical.

contrast_examples.jp: 雨が降るのを見ていた。

contrast_examples.en: As for Mei, her voice got lively. (main-clause topic)

prompt.context_jp: 隣に住んでるだけなのに 何で 私___悩まなくちゃならないの
prompt.prompt_jp: 何で 私___悩まなくちゃならないの
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits this 'why me?' exhaustive/identifying nuance?

feedback.correct_en: The 'why specifically ME of all people' meaning requires exhaustive-listing が — identifying who the sufferer is. は would just make it a casual topic statement.
feedback.incorrect_en: 私は悩まなくちゃならない would sound like a plain declaration ('I have to worry'), losing the indignant 'why ME?' focus.

contrast_examples.jp: 何で私がやらなきゃいけないの？
contrast_examples.en: Why do I have to do it? (exhaustive focus)

prompt.context_jp: ふと隣室のドアが開く気配がして、メイ___思わず身をこわばらせた。
prompt.prompt_jp: メイ___思わず身をこわばらせた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle marking Mei in the main clause.

feedback.correct_en: Mei is the established topic of this scene; her reaction is described from her ongoing perspective, so は fits. が would awkwardly introduce her as new information.
feedback.incorrect_en: メイが would suggest she is being newly identified, but the paragraph has been following her all along.

contrast_examples.jp: ドアが開いて、メイは驚いた。
contrast_examples.en: The door opened, and Mei (topic) was startled.

contrast_examples.jp: 誰が驚いたの？—メイが驚いた。

prompt.context_jp: ドアの向こうから顔を出したの___、髪を整え、ジャケットを羽織った田所だった。
prompt.prompt_jp: ドアの向こうから顔を出したの___、…田所だった。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for the cleft structure 'the one who...'.

feedback.correct_en: This is a cleft: 'The one who appeared was Tadokoro.' The nominalized clause is the topic (は), and the identification Tadokoro is the new info in the predicate.
feedback.incorrect_en: が here would blur the cleft structure; the standard '...のは Xだった' pattern uses は.

contrast_examples.en: The one who came was Tadokoro.

prompt.context_jp: 廊下の常夜灯だけ___、そのやり取りを静かに見下ろしていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 廊下の常夜灯だけ___、そのやり取りを…
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits the 'only X' exhaustive focus?

feedback.correct_en: 〜だけが emphasizes exhaustive identification: only the nightlight, and nothing else, was watching. が naturally pairs with だけ for this exclusive focus.
feedback.incorrect_en: だけは would imply contrast ('as for only the nightlight...'), which doesn't match the lonely-scene nuance here.

prompt.context_jp: 一方、廊下で___扉の向こうの気配を確かめる田所の視線が残っていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 一方、廊下で___扉の向こうの気配を…
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that signals contrast with the previous scene (Mei's room).

feedback.correct_en: 一方 signals a shift to a contrasting scene. で+は contrasts the hallway with Mei's room just described. This is classic contrastive は on a location.
feedback.incorrect_en: でが is ungrammatical. でに doesn't exist. Only では creates the needed contrast.

contrast_examples.jp: 東京では雨、大阪では晴れ。
contrast_examples.en: In Tokyo rain, in Osaka sunny. (contrast)
I played at the park. (neutral location)

prompt.context_jp: 前掛けを結んだ美登里の隣で、ナギサ___まな板の前に立ち、静かに包丁を持ち直していた。
prompt.prompt_jp: ナギサ___まな板の前に立ち…
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle introduces Nagisa into this new scene?

feedback.correct_en: Nagisa is being newly introduced into the kitchen scene as an observable actor. Descriptive narration of a scene uses が for new participants.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would treat Nagisa as the already-established topic, but the previous sentence was about Midori; Nagisa enters as fresh visual information.

contrast_examples.jp: 向こうからナギサが歩いてきた。
contrast_examples.en: Nagisa came walking from over there. (new info)

contrast_examples.jp: ナギサは料理が得意だ。
contrast_examples.en: Nagisa (as topic) is good at cooking.

prompt.context_jp: けれども、口調のなかにはっきりと角が立つのを、メイ___聞き逃さなかった。
prompt.prompt_jp: メイ___聞き逃さなかった。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle marking Mei as the perceiver.

feedback.correct_en: Mei is the chapter's established POV character. In a main-clause statement about what she noticed/didn't miss, は marks her as the ongoing topic.
feedback.incorrect_en: メイが would awkwardly single her out as if answering 'who didn't miss it?'—not the point here.

contrast_examples.jp: メイはそれに気づいた。
誰が気づいた？—メイが気づいた。

prompt.context_jp: ナギサという存在___、家族の外にいながら、いまや家の呼吸を知り尽くしていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: ナギサという存在___、家族の外にいながら…
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the particle for this characterizing statement about Nagisa.

feedback.correct_en: This is a characterizing/generic statement about Nagisa — 'As for Nagisa, he knows the household inside out.' That topic-comment structure needs は.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would narrow to a specific event ('Nagisa knew...') rather than the general characterization the sentence intends.

prompt.context_jp: 昔 サラリーマン___していた時 メイさんと同じような部下を 見ていました
prompt.prompt_jp: 昔 サラリーマン___していた時
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits 'was doing (the role of) X'?

feedback.correct_en: 〜をしている means 'to work as / play the role of X.' サラリーマンをする = be an office worker. を marks the role as the object of する.
feedback.incorrect_en: がしていた is ungrammatical. にしていた doesn't fit — に+する means 'decide on / turn into,' not 'work as.'

prompt.context_jp: この不均衡を放っておきたくないという気持ち___、彼女のなかで急速に膨らんでいった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 気持ち___、彼女のなかで急速に膨らんでいった。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for this newly-arising inner feeling.

feedback.correct_en: The feeling is a new, event-like phenomenon swelling up inside her — a classic 'something arises/grows' context that takes が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would frame the feeling as an already-known topic being commented on, losing the sense of it newly welling up.

contrast_examples.jp: 急に不安が湧いてきた。

prompt.context_jp: 夜が更けても、天井の木目を数えるほどに、メイ___寝つけずにいた。
prompt.prompt_jp: メイ___寝つけずにいた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle marking Mei in this descriptive line.

feedback.correct_en: Mei is the ongoing POV topic of the scene. Describing her continuing state (not sleeping) uses は.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would spotlight her identity as if newly introduced, which doesn't fit — she's been the focus all along.

contrast_examples.jp: 誰が眠れない？—私が眠れない。

prompt.context_jp: 眠らなければならないと思うほど、意識だけ___冴えていった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 意識だけ___冴えていった。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle captures the contrastive 'only consciousness (not sleep)' nuance?

feedback.correct_en: だけが with 冴える emphasizes exhaustive focus — of all things, only her mind grew sharper (while her body wanted sleep). This spotlight reading takes が.
feedback.incorrect_en: だけは would imply 'as for consciousness alone, (contrastively)...' — a weaker, more topic-setting nuance that doesn't fit the vivid descriptive flow.

contrast_examples.en: Only his eyes were shining. (vivid focus)

prompt.context_jp: 瀬川が車を取りに走り去り、通りには田所とメイのふたりだけ___残された。
prompt.prompt_jp: 田所とメイのふたりだけ___残された。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits 'only the two of them were left'?

feedback.correct_en: 'Only X was left' is an exhaustive identification of who remained — a canonical だけが pattern reporting an observable scene.
feedback.incorrect_en: だけは would introduce contrast with other groups, but here the point is simply identifying who remained on the street.

contrast_examples.jp: 教室には私だけが残った。
contrast_examples.en: Only I was left in the classroom.

contrast_examples.jp: 私だけは行きたくない。
contrast_examples.en: I alone don't want to go. (contrast)

prompt.context_jp: 田所___いつもの落ち着いた顔で腕を組み、その分析を頭のなかで整理しているようだった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 田所___いつもの落ち着いた顔で…
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle marking Tadokoro in this characterizing description.

feedback.correct_en: Tadokoro is the topic of this descriptive sentence about his habitual demeanor. は fits — 'As for Tadokoro, with his usual calm face...'
feedback.incorrect_en: が would spotlight him as new info, which clashes with the 'as usual' characterization.

contrast_examples.jp: 田所が急に立ち上がった。

prompt.context_jp: フロアの喧噪___、その一角だけ遠ざかったように感じられた。
prompt.prompt_jp: フロアの喧噪___、その一角だけ遠ざかった…
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the particle for this sensory/descriptive observation.

feedback.correct_en: Sensory descriptions of a phenomenon felt in the moment — the noise receding — take が to present it as a perceived event.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would turn the noise into a known topic being characterized, dulling the vivid 'felt as if' perception.

contrast_examples.jp: 風が冷たく感じられた。

prompt.context_jp: 告白の返事として:
prompt.prompt_jp: 「少し ___ ください」
prompt.prompt_en: Mei's reply to Higo-sensei's proposal: 'Please let me ___ a little.'

feedback.correct_en: 考えさせてください is the standard set phrase 'please let me think (about it)' — the causative-te + ください structure asks for permission.
feedback.incorrect_en: 考えてください means 'please think' (telling the other person to think). 考えられて is not idiomatic here.

contrast_examples.jp: 少し休ませてください。
contrast_examples.en: Please let me rest a bit.

prompt.context_jp: 私も28だしさ ___ような気持ちで 婚活してきたけど
prompt.prompt_jp: ___ような気持ちで 婚活してきた
prompt.prompt_en: Fill in the phrase meaning 'feeling cornered/pressured.'

feedback.correct_en: 追い詰められる = 'to be cornered/driven into a corner' — perfect for the desperate feeling of 婚活 (marriage-hunt) at 28.
feedback.incorrect_en: 追いかける = chase (active). 追い抜かれる = be overtaken. Neither captures the 'feeling pressured by time' nuance.

contrast_examples.jp: 時間に追い詰められている。

prompt.context_jp: 少しでも着任の可能性のある 先生を洗い出し 徹底的に ___に 調べておくんです
prompt.prompt_jp: 徹底的に ___に 調べておく
prompt.prompt_en: Fill in the idiom meaning 'exhaustively, leaving nothing out.'

feedback.correct_en: しらみ潰し ('crushing lice') = methodically going through every single one, leaving none out. Nagisa uses this military/sales metaphor.
feedback.incorrect_en: 虫食い = 'moth-eaten' (holes/gaps), the opposite nuance. 手当たり次第 means 'at random/whatever comes to hand,' which lacks the exhaustive-systematic nuance.

contrast_examples.jp: 手当たり次第に電話する。

prompt.context_jp: 情報戦ですか ___のチャンスですね
prompt.prompt_jp: ___のチャンスですね
prompt.prompt_en: Fill in the four-character idiom for 'winning by acting first.'

feedback.correct_en: 先手必勝 = 'first move, certain victory' — the one-who-moves-first wins. Fits the information-warfare context perfectly.
feedback.incorrect_en: 一石二鳥 = 'two birds one stone.' 七転八倒 = writhing in pain. Neither matches the 'act first to win' meaning.

contrast_examples.en: Let's go with 'strike first to win.'

prompt.context_jp: だからこそ ___の悔いのない人生を 目指すんだよ
prompt.prompt_jp: ___の悔いのない人生
prompt.prompt_en: Fill in to form the set phrase 'a life without a single regret.'

feedback.correct_en: 一片(いっぺん)の悔いもない/のない = 'not a single shred of regret' — a fixed literary expression Tadokoro uses to describe the ideal life.
feedback.incorrect_en: 一回 (one time) and 一本 (one stick/bottle) don't function as counters for abstract regret; the fixed collocation requires 一片.

prompt.context_jp: いつかは必ず 若い世代に___を 託さなければいけない時が来る
prompt.prompt_jp: 若い世代に___を 託さなければいけない
prompt.prompt_en: Fill in with the word meaning 'baton' in the passing-the-torch metaphor.

feedback.correct_en: バトンを託す = 'to entrust the baton' — the standard business/life metaphor for passing responsibility to the next generation.
feedback.incorrect_en: リレー is the relay itself, not the object passed. ゴール is the finish line, which can't be 'entrusted.'

contrast_examples.jp: 次の世代にバトンを渡す。
contrast_examples.en: Pass the baton to the next generation.

prompt.context_jp: このタイミングを ___わけにはいかないので 大切な思い出の日にしましょう
prompt.prompt_jp: このタイミングを ___わけにはいかない
prompt.prompt_en: Fill in the verb meaning 'to miss/let slip.'

feedback.correct_en: タイミングを逃す is the standard collocation 'to miss the timing/opportunity.' Combined with わけにはいかない = 'we can't afford to miss.'
feedback.incorrect_en: タイミングを落とす/抜く are not natural collocations. 落とす is used for dropping objects; 抜く for pulling out.

prompt.context_jp: 人生は決断の___、というよく聞くフレーズが…
prompt.prompt_jp: 人生は決断の___
prompt.prompt_en: Fill in to form the common phrase 'life is a ___ of decisions.'

feedback.correct_en: 決断の連続 = 'a succession/series of decisions' is the fixed idiomatic phrase.
feedback.incorrect_en: 続行 means 'continuation (of an action)' and 継続 means 'ongoing continuation' — neither forms the standard noun-of-N phrase here.

contrast_examples.en: Every day is a series of surprises.

prompt.context_jp: Higo-sensei's proposal to Mei:
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrasing sounds most natural for a sincere, formal 'will you go out with me?'

choices.text: 僕と つきあって いただけませんか？
僕と つきあって もらえない？

feedback.correct_en: いただけませんか is the humble, highly polite request form — fitting for a serious, marriage-minded proposal in a formal setting.
feedback.incorrect_en: もらえない？ is casual among close friends. つきあう？ is very blunt and casual, totally mismatched with 結婚を前提に.

contrast_examples.jp: 手伝っていただけませんか。
contrast_examples.en: Could you kindly help me? (very polite)

prompt.context_jp: ナギサがメイに自己紹介を頼まれたときの返答として:
prompt.prompt_en: Which response sounds most natural for Nagisa's polite, slightly deflecting reply?

choices.text: 少し お時間をください 次回までに ご用意いたします
少し 時間ちょうだい 次までに用意するよ
ちょっと待って 今度までに準備するから

feedback.correct_en: Nagisa consistently uses polite keigo (ご用意いたします, お時間を). It matches his professional housekeeper register with Mei.
feedback.incorrect_en: B and C are casual plain speech, which Nagisa never uses with Mei — it would break his characteristic formal distance.

prompt.context_jp: Mei's private muttering about not being able to sleep:
prompt.prompt_en: Which version sounds most natural as inner monologue/casual muttering?

choices.text: ヤバい ナギサさんのこと気になりすぎて 全然 眠れなかった
困りました ナギサさんのことが気になり 眠れませんでした
大変だ ナギサ氏について関心を持ちすぎ睡眠不可能だった

feedback.correct_en: Mei's private muttering uses casual register: ヤバい, 気になりすぎて, 全然眠れなかった — all natural informal speech fitting inner thought.
feedback.incorrect_en: B is overly polite masu-form, odd for talking to oneself. C uses stiff written vocabulary (ナギサ氏, 睡眠不可能) that no one would speak.

contrast_examples.jp: 困りました、眠れませんでした。
contrast_examples.en: I'm troubled, I couldn't sleep. (formal, odd alone)

prompt.context_jp: Tadokoro announcing his transfer:
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrasing is most natural for 'I've been put in charge as branch manager'?

choices.text: 支店長を任されることになってな
支店長を任せられる予定になっちゃった
支店長を任すことになったよ

feedback.correct_en: 任される (passive of 任せる) = 'to be entrusted/put in charge of.' 〜ことになって is the standard way to report an organizational decision.
feedback.incorrect_en: 任せられる予定になっちゃった is grammatically awkward and casual (ちゃった undercuts the gravity). 任す is the active form — he'd be the one assigning, not receiving.

contrast_examples.en: I was entrusted with an important role.
To entrust it to a junior.

prompt.context_jp: Yui reveals she's there as a housekeeper and asks to keep it secret:
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrasing fits Yui's professional-while-family tone with her father?

choices.text: 今日は私 家政婦として お仕事で来てるので お母さんには 絶対に秘密でお願いします
今日は家政婦で来てるんだから お母さんに言うなよ
本日は家政婦業務のため参上しておりますゆえ 母上には他言無用でございます

feedback.correct_en: A balances semi-polite (お仕事, 秘密でお願いします) with family warmth — appropriate when addressing her father while maintaining the housekeeper cover.
feedback.incorrect_en: B is too blunt/commanding to say to one's father in this emotional moment. C is comically archaic (参上, 母上, 他言無用) — totally out of place.
